$comment: The Semgrep step in .github/workflows/ci.yml carries no --exclude-rule flags. Every
dismissal lives here, and every dismissal names an owner, an expiry and a reason.
A finding with no entry fails CI. An entry past its expiry fails CI even though the
finding still matches, so an acceptance cannot outlive the triage that justified it.
An entry that matches nothing fails CI as stale — an acceptance nobody can point at
reads as reviewed when it is not.
Omit "paths" to accept a rule repository-wide. A "paths" entry matches an exact
repository-relative file, or a directory when the value ends in "/".
Triaged on 2026-08-17 against semgrep 1.172.0 with p/security-audit, p/typescript
and p/owasp-top-ten — the exact configuration the CI step runs.

entries.reason: Flags every actions/* reference by tag. scripts/check-action-pins.sh SHA-pins every THIRD-PARTY action and deliberately exempts GitHub's own first-party actions, which is a stricter policy than this rule and is itself enforced by check:ci-guardrails and .github/workflows/actions-pinned-check.yml.

The pwn-request shape in the deploy workflows. Each checkout is gated on github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository, which scripts/production-deploy-scope.test.mjs asserts for both workflows.

Test fixtures only. The values are synthetic and authenticate nothing; scripts/check-secrets.mjs is the blocking gate for real credential shapes. Scoped by path on purpose — the same rule firing in production code must fail.
ArtifactPreview routes markdown through DOMPurify and raw HTML through a sandboxed iframe; SEOHead emits ld+json and has no importers; ToolResultCard is under archive/ and is not built.

Supply-chain hardening worth doing: a cooldown is the defense against adopting a package compromised minutes after publication. It changes update cadence for every ecosystem in the file, so it lands as its own reviewed change rather than riding along with a security-gate edit.
Same supply-chain hardening track as the dependabot cooldown. A minimum release age changes what `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` will accept in CI, so it lands with its own install-behaviour review.
Same supply-chain hardening track as the dependabot cooldown. Both workspace files must move together or the two installs disagree.

Same supply-chain hardening track. An explicit trust policy blocks unreviewed postinstall scripts and will break installs for any dependency that currently relies on one, so it needs its own verification pass.
Same supply-chain hardening track. Blocking git/tarball sub-dependencies needs the resolved graph audited first — the Rust side already denies non-crates.io sources in deny.toml.
Same supply-chain hardening track, Python side. tools/skill-vetting resolves with uv and needs the same cooldown as the npm ecosystems.
